episode.title: Turn heterogeneous file-edit tool output into compact, reviewable chat diffs
episode.before: At first parent b9f302441fb3fc7927507ccd074a806d600b34d3, the desktop chat handled only write_file and edit_file as diff-producing tools, extracted only result.inline_diff, and rendered unified diffs as raw line-oriented blocks retaining file headers, hunk markers, and +/- markers. Patch results using result.diff were therefore not normalized into the same review surface, and file-edit rows could expose generic action labels or raw argument/result detail instead of a filename-centered review summary.
episode.after: At pinned merge commit 04a1d9efd76db1c5860bd5b928da95e37babb8b7, write_file, edit_file, and patch share one file-edit classification; diffs are accepted from inline_diff or diff; the view model derives basename/full-path metadata, suppresses redundant raw detail, and counts additions/removals. The disclosure row defaults open when a diff exists, shows a file-type icon, filename, path tooltip, and +N/-N statistics, and renders a bounded FileDiffPanel. The panel removes leading file metadata and hunk markers, strips diff markers while preserving change kind, applies add/remove accents, syntax-highlights recognized and budget-safe file types, and falls back to a plain colored renderer. Completed successful edit rows lacking a reviewable diff are hidden, while pending and failed edits remain visible.
episode.diff: Relative to first parent b9f302441fb3fc7927507ccd074a806d600b34d3, the pinned merge changes eight desktop files with 634 insertions and 80 deletions. The behavioral implementation centralizes file-edit recognition and result normalization in the tool view model, replaces the raw diff presentation with a parsed review panel, adds filename-to-icon/language resolution, integrates review metadata and disclosure behavior into the tool row, shares the Shiki theme with code blocks, and adjusts row/diff styling. Focused model tests were added for both accepted diff fields, patch-detail suppression, pending-path presentation, and exclusion of diff headers from line statistics.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned merge commit is 04a1d9efd76db1c5860bd5b928da95e37babb8b7 with first parent b9f302441fb3fc7927507ccd074a806d600b34d3 and subject "feat(desktop): PR-style file diffs in chat (#50731)".

Against its first parent, the pinned commit modifies eight desktop files with 634 insertions and 80 deletions, including the tool view model, tool fallback component, diff renderer, filename-language mapping, tests, and styles.

The after-state defines one file-edit classification containing edit_file, patch, and write_file, counts +/- lines while excluding +++/--- headers, and derives edit paths from arguments, result fields, or diff metadata.

The parent recognized only write_file and edit_file in relevant branches and inlineDiffFromResult read only inline_diff; the after-state routes patch through the same classification and accepts both inline_diff and diff.

For normalized file edits, the view model uses the basename as the dynamic title, preserves the path as subtitle, suppresses ordinary detail when a diff or path already conveys the result, and copies the diff preferentially.

The diff renderer removes leading Git/Hermes file-header metadata, drops hunk markers with separators between hunks, strips the leading diff marker, and retains add/context/remove kinds for line-level styling.

FileDiffPanel selects syntax highlighting from the file path only when a known language exists and the diff is within the highlight budget; otherwise it uses the plain change-colored renderer, while the asynchronous highlighting path also displays the plain renderer until ready.
Filename extension mapping supplies both shared file-type icons and bundled Shiki language identifiers, returning an empty language for unknown extensions so callers can fall back safely.

The chat tool row obtains live or persisted diffs, defaults the disclosure open when a diff exists, computes line statistics, shows filename/path-oriented metadata, and passes the normalized diff and path to FileDiffPanel.

A completed successful file-edit row with no diff is omitted as non-reviewable, but pending and error rows are retained; technical raw payload remains available behind a details disclosure when a diff is present.

Focused tests prove that both inline_diff and diff are accepted, a patch diff produces basename title plus full-path subtitle without raw patch detail, and a pending patch shows its path rather than argument JSON.
A focused test proves addition/removal statistics count actual changed lines while excluding unified-diff file headers.

The constituent implementation commits describe the intended behavior as a PR-style per-edit review, followed by filename-aware syntax highlighting with an unknown-language/over-budget/loading fallback and a shared lower-contrast dark theme.
The local evidence bundle identifies repository NousResearch/hermes-agent and issue/PR 50731 but reports the issue body, comments, timeline, PR body, reviews, and status checks as unavailable.

candidate_atomics.name: normalize-file-edit-review-data
candidate_atomics.title: Normalize file-edit results into one review model
candidate_atomics.description: Classify all supported mutation tools under one semantic role, reconcile live and persisted diff fields, derive stable file identity, suppress redundant payload detail, and calculate review statistics without counting diff metadata.

semantic_action.intent: Ensure every supported file mutation that carries a unified diff reaches the same review surface with concise identity and accurate change counts.
semantic_action.module_role: file-edit result adaptation and review-view modeling
semantic_action.pre_state: Mutation events may use different tool names and may place their unified diff in either a live side channel, inline_diff, or diff; generic formatting may expose raw arguments or fail to recognize the event as reviewable.
semantic_action.post_state: Recognized file mutations expose one normalized diff, basename title, full-path subtitle when available, empty redundant detail, and addition/removal counts that exclude file-header lines.
semantic_action.validation: Run the focused view-model tests asserting both diff-field variants, patch title/subtitle/detail behavior, pending-path behavior, and header-excluding line counts.

candidate_atomics.name: transform-unified-diff-for-review
candidate_atomics.title: Transform a unified diff into a readable review panel
candidate_atomics.description: Parse unified-diff structure into semantic line kinds, remove transport-oriented chrome, preserve code indentation, layer change accents over optional filename-derived syntax highlighting, and retain a bounded plain-renderer fallback.

semantic_action.intent: Make an edit diff readable as code review content rather than as raw patch protocol text, without making rendering depend on successful syntax highlighting.
semantic_action.pre_state: The available diff contains file headers, hunk coordinates, and +/- gutter markers and may have an unknown language, exceed the syntax-highlighting budget, or still be waiting for the highlighter.
semantic_action.post_state: Renderable lines omit leading file metadata and hunk coordinates, retain add/remove/context semantics and indentation, use bounded scrolling and change accents, and show syntax colors only when safely available while otherwise remaining readable in plain form.
semantic_action.validation: Render representative unified diffs and verify that header and hunk text are absent, changed lines retain their correct kind after marker removal, known budget-safe file paths use the syntax path, and unknown, over-budget, and loading states use the plain renderer.

candidate_atomics.name: integrate-diff-review-disclosure
candidate_atomics.title: Integrate diff review into navigable tool disclosures
candidate_atomics.description: Present each reviewable edit as an automatically expanded disclosure with file identity, change statistics, copy access, and raw technical drill-down, while omitting only settled successful rows that lack review content.

semantic_action.intent: Let a reviewer identify, open, scan, copy, and optionally inspect the raw payload of each file edit directly in the conversation without clutter from non-reviewable duplicates.
semantic_action.module_role: conversation review navigation and disclosure lifecycle
semantic_action.pre_state: File mutations appear as generic tool rows whose review content and identity are not consistently surfaced; rehydrated successful edits may leave empty duplicate rows.
semantic_action.post_state: A diff-bearing edit defaults open and exposes filename, path tooltip, file icon, +N/-N summary, bounded review panel, copy action, and optional technical payload; only completed successful edit rows with no diff are hidden, while pending and failed rows remain visible.
semantic_action.validation: Use the tested line-count helper for header statistics, then exercise the disclosure component with diff-bearing, pending, failed, and settled diff-less edit fixtures to verify open state, metadata, panel wiring, technical drill-down, and visibility rules.

candidate_workflows.name: convert-file-edit-events-into-reviewable-chat-diffs
candidate_workflows.title: Convert heterogeneous file-edit events into navigable code-review panels
candidate_workflows.description: A partial-order implementation workflow for adapting multiple mutation event shapes into a consistent, resilient diff-review experience embedded in a conversational tool stream.

workflow_graph.goal: Every supported file mutation carrying a unified diff is presented as a concise, navigable, and readable per-file review without exposing redundant raw payloads or depending on syntax-highlighter availability.
when_to_use: A conversational or activity-stream interface receives file mutations from multiple tool/event shapes and reviewers need to inspect the resulting code changes in place.
Mutation results already provide, or can be reconciled to, unified-diff text and a stable event identity.
Raw patch output currently includes transport metadata or generic tool payload detail that obscures the changed code.
anti_goals: Do not alter the semantics or contents of the underlying file mutation.
Do not count unified-diff file headers as additions or removals.
Do not require syntax highlighting for a diff to remain visible and readable.
Do not hide pending mutations or failed mutations merely because they lack a diff.
Do not remove access to raw diagnostic payloads when a technical drill-down mode is required.
not_applicable_when: The event has no file mutation semantics and no unified-diff representation.
The product requires an exact raw patch display including file headers, hunk coordinates, and +/- markers as its primary view.
The interface has no per-event disclosure or equivalent navigation surface in which review content can be presented.
inputs: Tool arguments and persisted result payloads
Optional live diff keyed by event/tool-call identity
workflow_graph.entry_state: File-edit events are rendered through generic tool-result formatting; supported names and diff fields are inconsistent, and raw unified-diff protocol text or argument JSON is exposed to the reviewer.
workflow_graph.exit_state: All admitted file-edit events with diffs use one normalized review contract and appear as filename-centered disclosures with accurate statistics and a resilient parsed diff panel; settled successful rows without review content are omitted without suppressing pending or error state.

steps.condition: Apply when a tool/event represents a file mutation and may expose a diff through live state, inline_diff, or diff.
steps.validation: Focused model tests accept both persisted fields, preserve the patch path during pending and completed states, suppress redundant detail, and return accurate +N/-N counts.

steps.condition: Apply when normalization yields non-empty unified-diff text.
steps.validation: Representative rendering proves removal of leading file headers and hunk coordinates, preservation of line kinds and indentation, and readable fallback behavior for unknown, over-budget, or loading highlighting states.

steps.condition: Apply in the conversation/activity row that owns disclosure, visibility, copy, and technical drill-down behavior.
steps.validation: Component fixtures verify default-open diff rows, filename/path/icon/stat metadata, FileDiffPanel wiring, retained technical payload access, and distinct visibility for pending, failed, diff-bearing, and settled diff-less events.

validation_ladder: Run focused pure-model tests for heterogeneous diff extraction, concise file identity, detail suppression, pending presentation, and line statistics.
Exercise parser/render fixtures covering Git headers, Hermes arrow headers, multiple hunks, context indentation, additions, removals, and empty lines.
Exercise highlighting branches for recognized filenames, unknown extensions, over-budget diffs, and the asynchronous loading fallback.
Exercise disclosure integration for live and rehydrated diffs, collapsed and expanded navigation, technical drill-down, pending activity, errors, and settled successful diff-less events.
Perform a manual light/dark visual review for readable syntax contrast, full-width change accents, bounded scrolling, keyboard focus, and unobstructed disclosure controls.
stop_conditions: Stop if no implementation-backed mapping from mutation events to unified-diff content can be established.
Stop rather than suppressing a row if it is pending or failed and no review diff is present.
Fall back to the plain renderer when filename language resolution fails, the rendering budget is exceeded, or highlighting is not ready.
Defer promotion if automated or manual evidence cannot establish that parsing preserves change kinds and disclosure navigation remains accessible.
unresolved_or_deferred: No dedicated automated tests for stripDiffFileHeaders, multi-hunk parsing, syntax-highlight fallback selection, disclosure interaction, keyboard navigation, or diff-less-row visibility were found in the pinned changed test set.
The checkout evidence does not include PR reviews, status checks, screenshots, or a recorded manual visual-validation result.
The focused tests were inspected at the pinned ref but were not executed because the active working tree does not materialize the pinned desktop application files or its dependency installation.

unresolved_questions: Did CI or manual review validate the untested renderer, disclosure, keyboard-focus, and dark/light visual behaviors? The issue bundle marks reviews and status checks unavailable.

Should successful rehydrated write_file/edit_file events persist their diff instead of being hidden when the diff side channel is unavailable? The implementation records this as a known persistence limitation rather than resolving it.

The merge includes an unrelated update-panel commit in its second-parent history; the ChangeEpisode excludes that behavior and scopes evidence to the eight files changed against the pinned merge's first parent.
